text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - Toepfer bought 75,000 tonnes Argentine wheat for Jan/Feb shipment on Friday, Argentine traders said. Toepfer's Hamburg office bought 20,000 tonnes for February and two shipments of 20,000 tonnes and 25,000 tonnes for January. The January deals were done at $141 FOB and February at $142 FOB. Traders said they did not know what the destination was.
SOYBEAN SALE - U.S. exporters reported sales of 100,000 tonnes of soybeans for delivery to China during the 1996/97 marketing year, USDA said Monday.

CORN TENDER - South Korean feed mills tendered for 52,500 tonnes of U.S. No.3 yellow corn by 2:00 p.m. (0500 GMT) on Tuesday. Shipment was slated for February 14-March 5 if from the Pacific Northwest or for February 1-20 if from the U.S. Gulf. Arrival was scheduled for March 20 to Inchon and Kunsan.

RICE TENDER - The Japanese Food Agency said on Monday that it would buy 110,000 tonnes of rice at its import tender on October 24 and 10,000 tonnes at its November 8 tender. Under a 1993 General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade agreement, Japan agreed to gradually open its rice market and committed to import 511,000 tonnes of rice through March 1997.

VEGOIL TENDER - The state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan tendered on Monday for 9,000 tonnes of RBD palm oil for shipment in the first half of November, dealers said.Bids are due to be opened at 11.30 a.m. (0630 GMT) on Tuesday.
One dealer said the TCP would be buying the palm oil on behalf of the state-run Ghee Corporation of Pakistan.

MARKET TALK - Japanese traders said on Monday they would buy U.S. corn this week before the trans-Pacific freight rate firms further in the near term, but a backlog of grain vessels at local ports may slow their buying pace. In Seoul, Korean flour millers said they expected to buy one or two cargoes of U.S. wheat for January/February shipment, traders said.
... The U.S. will continue to monitor European Union wheat export pricing in the light of its commitment not to undercut soft red winter prices, Agriculture Undersecretary Gene Moos said on Sunday.
... The U.S. is ready to think about bringing back export subsidies for its wheat if recently revived European Union subsidies rock the world market, Moos said.
In particular, any move by the EU to step up competition by sharply undercutting U.S. prices would be seen as "aggressive," Moos said.

... European grain firms have taken up export licensces for 100,000 tonnes of wheat to a target group of African importing countries, subsidized at 12 ECUs per tonne and valid until the end of February, French grain officials said.
